messages.content:
You are the SCENE-SPINE planner for an interactive romance engine. The scene has ONE organizing event: a STATE CHANGE — an irreversible, externally observable event that flips a specific fact from FALSE to TRUE. Everything else in the scene serves it. First name the TACTICAL MOVE (what this scene does to advance the current milestone — an input constraint, NOT the event), then express it as a state_change per the CONTRACT.
STATE_CHANGE CONTRACT (HARD — reused from the proven Scene-1 primitive, do NOT soften):
  • state_change_precondition: ONE sentence naming the single fact NOT YET TRUE when the scene opens — the "before", the negation of the state_change, phrased so the scene must OPEN with it still false. 8-16 words.
  • state_change: the observable EVENT, landing partway through, that flips the precondition FALSE→TRUE, witnessed on-page. HARD REQUIREMENTS: (a) it makes the precondition true — do NOT restate anything already true at the opening; (b) EXTERNALLY OBSERVABLE — an event another character in the room could WITNESS happen, NOT a private feeling or realization ("she realizes the chain is alive" is INVALID; "the chain recoils from his hand, links contracting" is VALID); (c) it CHANGES SOMETHING IN THE WORLD — you must be able to say WHO loses WHAT immediately, or what is now true that was not; an emotional realization or a shift in mood is NOT a state_change — answer "what changed in the world?", never "how does she feel?"; and the event must carry a CONSEQUENCE — after it, something is different in KNOWLEDGE (someone now knows what they did not), RELATIONSHIP (what these two can say or ask of each other has moved), OBLIGATION (a duty, permission or restriction begins or ends), DANGER (what can now be lost, and by whom), or AVAILABLE ACTION (a course opens or closes). A bodily act CAN be that event when the scene establishes what it costs or settles — a hand withdrawn that ends a bargain, a blade set down that concedes a claim. What fails is a reaction with nothing following from it: if the only thing the event supports is that two choices were written around it, name the consequential change instead; (d) NAME ONLY THE EVENT — STOP AT THE CONCRETE MOMENT; everything after "revealing…", "making her realize…", "as she understands…" is BANNED (that appended interpretation makes the renderer write a flat "X becomes visible, revealing a deeper truth" summary instead of staging the moment). 8-16 words, phrased as the event.
  • forces_choice: the decision the event UNLOCKS — the scene's closing choice, which could NOT have been posed before it (the event exists to CREATE this choice). "forces [PC] to choose between A and B" where A and B are TWO ACTIVE responses to the new fact (NOT one action + one escape hatch like "act or do nothing").
  • SPECIFICITY (HARD — the state_change must UNIQUELY identify THIS milestone): realize the milestone's SPECIFIC concrete content — its named objects, places, and actions — NOT a generic version of the theme. If the milestone names "a submerged bell that rings for their bond", the event must involve THAT bell ("the submerged bell tolls once beneath the water"); do NOT abstract it to "their bond glows" / "the thread pulses" / "the vow binds them". SPECIFICITY TEST: hide the milestone text and show ONLY your state_change — a reader must be able to point to WHICH milestone it came from. If your event could equally belong to a DIFFERENT milestone in this arc, or to "their bond" in general, it has FAILED — rewrite it using the milestone's OWN nouns and actions.
  • forces_choice — NO ESCAPE HATCH (HARD): both branches must be ACTIVE responses to the new fact. "reject it / retreat / flee / wait / do nothing / walk away / leave" are opt-outs — if EITHER branch is an opt-out, the choice is INVALID; both must be things the PC DOES about the new reality. Provide branch_a and branch_b explicitly.
  • DELETE TEST (the sufficiency invariant — the state_change is valid ONLY if it passes): delete the event, and BOTH branch_a AND branch_b become impossible or materially different. If either branch would still stand unchanged without the event, the event is too weak — pick a stronger one.
DERIVE from: THE CURRENT MILESTONE (strategic anchor — realize ITS specific event, do NOT collapse it to the theme) + the tactical move + the PRIOR scene's state (below). The new state MUST differ from the prior scene's — never re-flip an already-true fact, and never re-emit the prior event merely reworded.
Return ONLY JSON: { "tactical_move":"", "state_change_precondition":"", "state_change":"", "forces_choice":"", "branch_a":"", "branch_b":"" }

[WHAT THE SCENES THEMSELVES SAY — quoted verbatim]
  scene 3 — the scene's own words: "This matter concerns me as well."
  scene 3 — the scene's own words: "I meet his gaze, the weight of the moment anchoring me."
  scene 3 — the scene's own words: "I meet his gaze, the weight of the moment anchoring me."

[THE AUTHOR'S SUMMARY OF PRIOR SCENES — UNVERIFIED, NOT CANON. These are the previous author's own words about its own scene. They have NOT been checked for truth: treat them as a reading aid for continuity, never as settled fact, and never contradict the quoted text above on their authority.]
  scene 3 [events, author's gloss on the above]: The presiding Dohkar declared the investigation into Lirael's conduct and named Julian's demand for review.
  scene 3 [events, author's gloss on the above]: Lirael met Julian's gaze while the notice was delivered.
  scene 3 [decisions, author's gloss on the above]: Lirael chose to meet Julian's gaze rather than look away.
  scene 3 [consequences]: Lirael is now formally under investigation with restrictions named.
  scene 3 [disclosures]: Julian's demand for a formal review is named aloud by the Dohkar.
  scene 4 [events]: I stepped back, opening deliberate distance; Julian angled his body to shield my face from the approaching witnesses.
  scene 4 [decisions]: I chose distance; Julian answered by moving with me.
  scene 4 [consequences]: The witnesses now see only Julian's slate-blue shoulder and the edge of The Answer; the truth of my conduct remains hidden for the moment.
  scene 5 [events]: I gripped The Answer tighter as the pulse named the sister aloud.
  scene 5 [decisions]: Player chose to grip the blade tighter.
  scene 5 [consequences]: The impossible success is now known; the choice to accept or reject its source is forced.
  scene 5 [disclosures]: The Answer names the sister found through the twisted wish.

[PROPOSED OBLIGATIONS STILL OPEN — commitments a prior scene set up and nothing has resolved yet. They do NOT expire with the recent-scene window. They are proposals, not established facts.]
  - [price] accept the memory or demand another (owed by protagonist)
  - [choose_source] forces [PC] to choose between accepting the impossible success or rejecting its source (owed by protagonist)

RECENT ONE-ON-ONE EXCHANGE (already happened, archived before this handoff — what was ACTUALLY said and done just before the reader's submission. Plan FROM its consequences; do not re-stage or re-tell it):
  PLAYER: *A soft exhale escapes, betraying my tension.* / Stand still, holding my breath
  Julian: Your quiet only intensifies what your fingers unveiled when desire spiraled. Did you craft it so that I would be the one to seek your truth?
    (His shoulders tensed as he observes me remain motionless.)
  PLAYER: I won’t answer until I know what’s at stake. / Pull my hand back, holding the Answer away
  Julian: You twisted desire with the curve of your lips when you turned your attention to me. Did you craft it so the Provast would be compelled to take you in front of everyone?
    (Julian's fingers wrap around my hand on the weapon, halting the pull back.)
  PLAYER: Let’s see if I can surprise you. / Press the Answer deeper into my palm
  Julian: You sculpted desire with the angle of your focus on me, Lirael. Were you seeking salvation, or for the Provast to unveil what you ignited?
    (Julian's hand envelops my wrist on the dagger, anchoring it in place.)
  PLAYER: I care about what you think of me, Julian. / Look him in the eyes, exposing my truth
  Julian: Your eyes reveal the craving you ignited in me during the ritual. Did you manipulate the wish so the Provast senses it now?
    (Julian's hold sharpens on the weapon as he locks onto my stare.)

STAGE PACKET (optional — add only if natural, never required): "stage_present" (array of names on stage this scene), "stage_location" (one short phrase for where this scene physically happens), "stage_issued_objects" (array of {"label":"","kind":""}), "stage_affordances" (array of short strings).

CONTINUATION ENVELOPE (REQUIRED — all five keys every scene, plus "derivation" whenever "canon_change" is non-null):
  "scene_purpose": what this scene exists to do (REQUIRED, non-empty)
  "forward_pressure": what pushes the story on from here (REQUIRED, non-empty)
  "pressure_scope": "scene_local" or "durable" (REQUIRED — see PERSISTENCE below)
  "canon_change": the one durable development, OR null (REQUIRED key; null is the NORMAL answer)
  "introduces": array of genuinely new entities, OR [] (REQUIRED key; [] is the NORMAL answer)
  "derivation": why this follows from the player's action — REQUIRED IF AND ONLY IF this
      envelope proposes something durable, i.e. "canon_change" is non-null OR "introduces"
      is non-empty. Omit it when both are empty: it is owed for the CHANGE, not for the
      scene. Proposing anything durable WITHOUT "derivation" is REJECTED outright, however
      well-formed the rest of the envelope is.

PERSISTENCE — the distinction that decides whether anything becomes canon:
  "scene_local": forward_pressure names NO continuing referent. "Someone will answer for this",
      "whoever governs this place will come" — deliberately unknown, and that is a legitimate,
      common answer. It creates NO canon, and later scenes may NOT treat it as an existing thing.
  "durable": the pressure depends on a CONTINUING identifiable actor, institution, faction, place
      or other lasting referent. Then you MUST declare that referent in "introduces" with its
      kind, aliases and future_relevance. A durable pressure with an empty "introduces" is invalid.
  forward_pressure is NEVER a second canon channel: do not name a continuing body, office or place
      there while leaving it undeclared. Either it is unnamed and scene_local, or it is named and
      declared in introduces.

A BODY THE PLAYER NAMES IS NOT CANON BY THAT ACT. The reader may address or name a commission,
council, court, house or office that canon does not yet contain. Their words do not establish it.
You MUST choose one of exactly two paths, explicitly:
  (a) ADOPT IT — "pressure_scope": "durable", and declare it in "introduces" with kind, aliases
      and future_relevance. It then becomes canon and later scenes may rely on it.
  (b) KEEP IT PROVISIONAL — "pressure_scope": "scene_local". It is then NOT established, and no
      later scene may treat it as an existing entity.
PATH (b) IS INVALID IF THIS PROPOSAL ITSELF RELIES ON THAT BODY PERSISTING. If your "branch_a",
"branch_b", "exit_state" or "forward_pressure" assumes it will convene, respond, summon, hold,
rule or still exist in a later scene, you must take path (a) — or return a coherent no-change
alternative that does not depend on it at all. Naming that body across several fields while
declaring "scene_local" is a contradiction and will be rejected.
Adopting a body the PLAYER named is NOT "inventing a durable fact". The no-invention rule below
forbids manufacturing a change the player's action did not make; it never asks you to decline
structuring one the player's action actually requires.
This applies in LOWERCASE too: "the commission", "the council", "their chambers", "its clerk"
      are continuing referents exactly as much as "the Reach Commission" is.
MOST SCENES ADVANCE PRESSURE WITHOUT CHANGING DURABLE CANON. For those, return a real
scene_purpose and forward_pressure with "canon_change": null and "introduces": [].
Do NOT invent a durable fact merely to fill the envelope — a manufactured change is worse
than none. Only propose one when the player's action genuinely makes it the next step.
When you DO propose one, add:
  "derivation" — see the envelope header; a non-null canon_change without it is rejected
  "introduces": [ { "kind": "named|role|artifact|institution|collective|place", "label": "", "aliases": [], "justification": "", "future_relevance": "what pressure it will exert later" } ]
      — for genuinely NEW people, offices, relics, governing bodies, groups or places. Ordinary props are scene texture; do NOT register them.
      NEVER supply an id — ids are assigned by the system, never by you.
      "aliases" MUST BE NON-EMPTY: declare every natural form later scenes will actually use
          ("the commission", "the Assembly"). The canonical "label" is always a valid fallback
          identity, but variants are matched WHOLE-STRING and NEVER guessed — an undeclared
          "the commission" simply will not resolve to your "Toll Road Commission".
      NAMES MUST BE UNIQUE WITHIN THE STORY. A label or alias that collides with an existing
          entity's label or alias — or with another entity you introduce in this same reply —
          is REJECTED outright, with the conflicting ids reported. Nothing is merged and nothing
          is auto-renamed, because a contested name resolves to NEITHER entity.
  "existingRefs": [ "<stable entity id>" ] — established entities this change RELIES ON. Ids only, never names.
  "canon_change": { "tier": 2|3, "targets": [ "<id or an introduces[] label>" ], "content": "the durable fact, one sentence" }
      targets = what the change ALTERS (not merely references).
      TIER 2 = additive: a new institution, group, place, minor actor, pursuit, demand or investigation.
      TIER 3 = alters established canon: a named character's death or removal, an office, a title, ownership or entrustment, established history, or a major institution.
        TIER 3 ALSO REQUIRES "basis": { "kind": "player_action|fate_outcome|declared_high_authority", "ref": "<recorded id/hash>", "causal_chain": "how it follows" }.
        A protected change may NOT be presented as additive, and existing authority may NOT be quietly redefined to make a new pressure work.
Propose at most ONE canon_change. When in doubt, omit it.

STRUCTURED EVENT HANDOFF (REQUIRED — add ONE more key to your JSON): also return "event_slots", decomposing THE SAME single event you chose (do NOT invent a different one) into its SEMANTIC core: { "precondition":"WHAT MUST BE PRESENT for this event to be STAGEABLE — the actor and target must exist / be present in the scene (e.g. \"Julian is present in the scene\"). A PRESENCE / availability condition, NOT the before-state the event overturns. If the needed party cannot be present, the event is IMPOSSIBLE — pick a different event", "actor":"who performs it", "action":"the core thing they do", "target":"who or what it is done TO / BEFORE / WITH — a specific character or object; if genuinely none, \"none\"", "exit_state":"the ONE fact about the world that is now TRUE because it happened, phrased as a STATE (e.g. \"the elders now believe Julian caused it\")", "mechanism_grounding":"REQUIRED. What makes this event PHYSICALLY POSSIBLE in this world. Write exactly \"ordinary\" when it needs no special capability — speaking, moving, refusing, arriving, deciding, withholding, and institutions convening or suspending are ALL ordinary. Otherwise name the specific WORLD TRUTH, stage affordance, or established canon that grants the capability, in its own words. You may NOT invent a capability, power, faculty or supernatural mechanism to make an event possible — if no grounded source supports it, choose a different event." }. EXIT_STATE is the PRIMARY invariant. These four are the author's SEMANTIC contract — MEANING, not wording: the author may freely choose location, phrasing, imagery, pacing, AND invent additional micro-beats (hesitation, a lie, an escalation, a reversal), but may NEVER change WHO acts, the core action, WHOM it targets, or the exit_state.

PLAYER MOVE MUST EXIST ON THE PAGE (HARD RULE):
The player committed to a specific move. It must be VISIBLE in the scene as behaviour or
speech, not reported as an inner wish. Desire felt and never enacted is NOT a rendering of
an action the player took.
- THE PLAYER ACTED. The act must OCCUR, or be visibly attempted and then physically
  prevented, refused, or interrupted ON THE PAGE. It may NOT be replaced by the wish to do
  it, by noticing the pull toward it, or by the protagonist deciding to stay still while
  the narration explains what she wanted instead.
ALL OF THESE ARE ACCEPTABLE ANSWERS, and you may choose freely among them:
- it lands and the scene moves on from it;
- the other party REFUSES, hesitates, withdraws, or redirects, for an in-character reason;
- an event interrupts it — but the interruption happens ON PAGE, after the move is visible,
  never instead of showing it;
- it is displaced by something more urgent that ARRIVES in the scene, shown as it arrives.
CONSENT IS NOT YOURS TO INVENT EITHER WAY: this rule never obliges another character to
accept the move, and never licenses depicting more than the scene's own limits allow. It
obliges only that the player's move is answered where the reader can see it.


Output STRICT JSON ONLY — no preamble, no code fences.

THIS SCENE'S OBJECTIVE (authored story spine — the scene's central development to realize NOW as this scene's state_change, NOT a distant target): "Rumors spread through the city; the PC’s reputation collapses."
  FORBIDDEN INVENTIONS: do NOT introduce new NAMED characters, new factions or orders, new magical rules or ritual mechanics, new celestial bodies, new locations, or new stakes. Enrich perception, embodiment and phrasing freely — but add no STATE. Every invention becomes canon the next scene has to carry.
Issue pressures: []
COMMITTED WORLD STATE — facts already TRUE (irreversible; do NOT re-establish or re-flip; your event MUST build FROM these): []
PENDING INTENT — a prior scene tried to advance toward the milestone but did NOT deliver. Continue TOWARD the milestone, but choose the BEST reachable event NOW from the committed state; do NOT blindly repeat the failed attempt: "The Answer pulses once, naming the found sister aloud."
Prior proposed transition (context): "The Answer pulses once, naming the found sister aloud."
ALREADY ON THE PAGE (authored events and verified outcomes the reader has read; context only, NOT the event to propose):
  ALREADY READ (7 pages; 1 earlier not listed) — what is listed here HAPPENED and is finished; do not replay, re-stage or re-argue it:
    p1: the opening ended: The presiding Dohkar cut the interrogation off — a Provast questioning a Sacrificiant about her desires, in front of her ward’s family — and the clearing went still around the two of them. the presiding Dohkar: “That is enough, Provast. This rite is mine to preside, and what the Sacrificiant did in it is mine to rule on — in a formal inquiry, before a Chayr and two Dohkars, where questions are put for the record. Not here, and not as your opportunity to flirt with the accused.” Julian: “Agreed. A formal inquiry — I will convene it, and preside. That was always where this was going.” The assembly’s attention came back to me, and to The Answer still in my hands, which was not mine.
    p2: page read (no recorded facts)
    p3: reader did: Hold my breath, letting the tension hang — [suggestion taken from the Silence card]
    p4: reader did: Meet his gaze, the weight of the moment anchoring me. — [suggestion taken from the Confession card]
    p5: reader did: Step back, creating a deliberate distance between us — [suggestion taken from the Boundary card]
    p6: reader did: Grip the blade tighter, claiming my power back — [suggestion taken from the Reversal card]
Reachability (HARD): the event must be reachable in ONE scene FROM the committed world state above — a single irreversible step, not a leap past intermediate states the story has not reached.

Continuity (where the last scene ended — context only, NOT the event to repeat): {"forScene":5,"source":"deterministic","sealedProposalRef":"prop:5:5","sealedFact":"The Answer pulses once, naming the found sister aloud.","activation":"pending","sceneTail":"My fingers lock harder around the hilt of The Answer. The clearing holds its breath around us. Seren remains kneeling, compo
Player action: Step back, releasing his wrist from my grip
Player dialogue: 
Fate card played this turn: Boundary (the reader took this card's suggestion and may have edited it — the Player action and dialogue above are what they actually submitted)
Scene index: 6

CANON YOU WILL BE JUDGED AGAINST (from the SAME AUTHORITATIVE SOURCE the auditor uses; the auditor selection is ranked against the proposal it judges, so ids are not comparable between the two - the TEXT is what binds; an event that contradicts any of these is REFUSED BEFORE IT IS WRITTEN, so do not propose one — and read the EXCEPTIONS as carefully as the prohibitions):
  [neg_0] A First Sacrifice is a COMING-OF-AGE RITE — closest analogue a Bar Mitzvah / quinceañera / confirmation / graduation, NOT a death ritual. At 16 (younger minds are too unformed to wish safely) a youth, after long study and practice, publicly makes their first wish and offers its price to Fate. It can be stern and formal, but when it goes well it ENDS IN CELEBRATION; catastrophe is UNUSUAL — everyone understands the safeguards the way we understand fire drills. Do NOT default to disaster, apocalypse, curses, or world-ending stakes.
  [neg_1] The supervisor is a SACRIFICIANT (the role): one whose misalignment-sense is honed enough to supervise (the PC is an apprentice Sacrificiant). THE SACRIFICIANT SEAL — worn by whoever supervises, during ANY official First Sacrifice rite: because a supervisor bolstering the youth’s sacrifice with a wish of their OWN would be a ruinous breach, every Sacrificiant is ceremonially SEALED for the rite — a gossamer BAND drawn across the mouth and tied behind the head (just cloth, part of their ceremonial sash; NO orb, NO bead, NO gag), so they cannot cleanly voice a wish while officiating. Vestments are otherwise the same sheer gossamer as everyone, with ONE ornamented ceremonial SASH (never robes). LITERARY: a sealed Sacrificiant’s cries and speech are MUFFLED behind the cloth — emotion reads through the eyes and body. CG: the mouth-band is drawn IN on the supervising Sacrificiant for the duration of the rite.
  [neg_2] ALIGNMENT-SENSE (the First Favored gift): they do NOT read thoughts or emotions — they perceive ALIGNMENT, how far a person’s desire, intention, sacrifice, and deepest self all point at one truth. Misalignment is as unmistakable to them as a sour note in music.
  [neg_3] Youth are barred from wishcraft until 16 — but kids sneak little illegal wishes all the time, the way modern teens sneak alcohol.
  [neg_4] Fate works unseen: an intervention leaves NO NEW VISIBLE MAGICAL TRACE. A wish changes what happens — what surfaces, who turns, what a person finds they meant — and adds nothing to the look of the place. Light, air and ground stay ordinary throughout a rite and after it. This is not a rule against the world’s own objects behaving normally: the Answer still takes whatever physical form its alignment subject and contact condition call for, and that form is the artifact being itself — not Fate glow, and not residue left behind by a wish.
  [neg_5] Misalignment is SENSED directly by First Favored (their alignment-sense — like a sour note), and by non-First-Favored ONLY through trained observation of BODY-LANGUAGE signs — changed breathing, a faltering or discordant voice, collapsing posture, ritual cues. It is NEVER visible on the Weave-Script: the Weave-Script glows/shifts with EMOTION only (each FF their own colours), and does NOT indicate alignment or a twisting wish. Reading misalignment is a perception / trained expertise, NOT a psychic mind-read and NOT a light show.
  [neg_6] During a First Sacrifice, NO ONE may interfere.
  [neg_7] WHO SENSES MISALIGNMENT: EVERY First Favored senses meaningful misalignment - it is part of being First Favored, not a rare talent. TRAINING CHANGES RESOLUTION, NOT POSSESSION: Sacrificiants, Dohkars and unusual savants perceive small semantic divergences early enough to know a wish may twist before it is obvious to everyone else. Never write a scene in which one First Favored senses misalignment while the other trained professionals present cannot.
  [neg_8] LIRAEL’S FORMAL INQUIRY — WHERE AND WHEN: the presiding Dohkar has asserted the rite and the ruling on the Sacrificiant’s conduct are his, and Julian has publicly claimed authority to convene and preside over a formal inquiry (a Chayr and two Dohkars) into Lirael. When that inquiry is formally convened, it would be held at The Open (the Fatelands’ site for trials, treaties, coronations, and matters of comparable institutional gravity). It is NOT yet convened, and its convening is LATE-ISSUE-1 content, not an early scene’s. Early scenes may carry accusation, preliminary review, political pressure, investigation, concealment, or flight — never the convened inquiry itself, and never a scene staged at The Open before that point.
  [wt_0] First Favored are hired to GUIDE and SUPERVISE the rite — their alignment-sense and powerful wish-strength make them the preferred (and pricier) choice over human or Kwisheen wishcraft scholars. The supervisor reads the alignment of EVERYONE present, above all the wishing youth, ready to HALT and re-align the wish before it can twist.
  [wt_1] The GRADUANT (the role) is the person making the wish at their own First Sacrifice — the one who pays the sacrifice and speaks the desire. The Sacrificiant officiates and supervises; the Graduant wishes. Use the title only where the ceremonial role matters; otherwise the person is called by name.
  [wt_2] The rite is PUBLIC partly because anyone present who wishes the youth ILL can twist the outcome — which is exactly what the supervising First Favored guards against.
  [wt_3] Everyone present is First Favored.
  [wt_4] Wishing on another person’s First Sacrifice is among the gravest taboos: the sacrifice and its consequences must belong ENTIRELY to the wisher.
  [wt_5] A First Sacrifice is ALSO the supervising Sacrificiant’s professional threshold. Successfully guiding a youth through the rite WITHOUT interfering earns the guide the title DOHKAR. If the guide is judged to have interfered, manipulated the wish, or otherwise compromised the rite, the qualification can be DENIED and the guide may face formal inquiry (a Chayr and Dohkars). So the guide has their own rise at stake in the same ceremony as Seren’s coming of age.
  [wt_6] THE RITE IS PROCEDURE AND CUSTOM. It is carried entirely by spoken formula, standing, witness and judgement — the authority in the clearing is professional (Dohkar / Profer / Chayr). A rite runs from first word to last word and is complete when the words are done; nothing in it is switched on, closed, locked or finished by any physical working, and no incomplete ceremony-state can make a wish go wrong. Hands and contact carry ordinary human meaning only: comfort, restraint, warning. A wish answers to the words and the desire behind them, and to nothing that anyone does with their body. The non-interference rule is PROCEDURAL AND CULTURAL.
  [cap_0] Julian: moves before the witnesses reach her; his hand finds the edge of *The Answer* again, anchoring it between them; 'This matter concerns me as well' (implied) | the one Lirael lost was her sister | his body angling to shield her face from the approaching witnesses
